text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- PLASTICS MARKET ATTRACTS INVESTMENT
This year should be the seventh consecutive year in which there has been a growth in the consumption of plastics, a market which is growing three times as fast as gross domestic product.
-- KANDIR SAYS GDP SHOULD GROW 5 PERCENT
Planning Minister Antonio Kandir told an audience in Barcelona that Brazil's economy should grow five percent this year and by an average of 6.5 percent over the next 10 years.
-- SOY PRICES RISE 11.6 PERCENT IN LAST 30 DAYS
Soy prices rose 11.6 percent over the past 30 days on rumors the Brazilian government is going to create an export tax that would effect the market.
O GLOBO
-- LATIN AMERICA GROWS 3.1 PERCENT IN 1996

Latin America's economy grew 3.1 percent in 1996, compared to just 1.0 percent the year before, according to a study by the Inter-American Development Bank. The bank will release its findings today in Barcelona.
-- BRAZIL'S IRS ASKS U.S. FOR HELP IN CORRUPTION PROBE
Brazil's internal revenue service has requested help from the United States in an ongoing corruption probe involving former Brazilian President Fernando Collor and his top aide.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
--- PC FARIAS USED CAYMAN ISLAND BANK TO HIDE FUNDS
Paulo Cesar Farias, the late aide to former President Fernando Collor, used the Cayman Island bank Trade Link Bank to hide illicit funds.
-- INTEREST ON FOREIGN, DOMESTIC DEBT TO HIT $25.2 BLN
Interest payments on official foreign and domestic debt will reach $25.2 billion this year, or 12 percent of the federal budget, compared to 8.7 percent for health and 5.5 percent for education.
* Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
((--John Miller, Sao Paulo newsroom, 5511 248-5414))
